focus: standalone skills cli-orca, sk-git, sk-prompt, sk-vision
noveltyJustification: The Class S contract and the three divergent router implementations are new evidence; the duplication pattern itself was already established, so the ratio is below iteration 1.
ruledOut: A per-mode ROUTER.md for standalone skills
Treating the four standalone routers as interchangeable

label: All four roots are Class S by the fleet contract: mode-registry, hub-router, description and command-metadata are forbidden, leaf-manifest.config is required, leaf-manifest and leaf-aliases are generated; the contract lists exactly these seven S roots.

sk-vision's router cannot route: one intent maps to two directory prefixes and route_resources loads every markdown file under them, so INTENT_SIGNALS never selects and UNKNOWN_FALLBACK fires only on an empty corpus.
cli-orca declares per-intent weights that its router never reads (lane selection counts matched phrases at line 177), and it carries a unique FOREIGN_OWNERS cross-skill ownership map.

sk-git implements a third scoring shape with NOISY_SYNONYMS and a boundary-aware keyword matcher, so the fleet's 'weighted intent scoring' has three different implementations and only sk-git fixes the substring bug.
sk-prompt forbids duplicated routing lookup tables in a comment at lines 56-57, then lists the leaf files three times and adds a fourth mode-selection table (COMMAND_INTENTS).

Standalone routing bounds duplication at two files because description.json is forbidden: advisor vocabulary lives only in graph-metadata.json and the SKILL.md block, unlike the hub's five-way restatement.

Routing dominates every standalone file: sk-prompt spends 215 of 524 lines (41%) in section 2 before the first instruction, sk-git has a 2,195-character rule at line 307, and cli-orca a 673-character paragraph at line 226.
